# Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta (Iti 19 (It 1.19 PTS It 11))

**ID:** Iti 19 (It 1.19 PTS It 11)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta* (Iti 19, PTS It 11) is the nineteenth discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, located in its first section (*Ekakanipāta*). The discourse teaches that concord and unity within the monastic community (*saṁgha*) lead to the welfare, benefit, and happiness of many beings, both human and divine. It culminates in a verse declaring that harmony in the community is blissful, and that whoever reunites a split community generates vast merit and rejoices in heaven for an eon (*kappam saggamhi modati*) [La Vallée Poussin 1988].

In Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (ad IV.124), the six *pāda*s of this verse from Iti 19 are cited following a passage from the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10.40, PTS AN v 76) to illustrate that reconciling a schismatic assembly constitutes "Brahma-merit" (*brāhma puṇya*), bearing the fruit of celestial bliss for an entire cosmic period [La Vallée Poussin 1988].
